evidence.curator_note: The book CROSSES OUT the reaction arrow of equation 4.16 (a large X is printed over it): allylic-type cleavage is disfavored at a carbonyl double bond because the product's resonance stabilization requires positive charge on a MONOVALENT oxygen, the partner canonical form being the extremely unstable alpha-acylcarbonium ion (Dommroese 1987); the trivalent oxonium (acylium) route of equation 4.14 wins. The printed abundance is '0.5% (C3H5O+ = 100%)', i.e. this C4H7O+ ion is 0.5% of the m/z 57 acylium base peak of 3-pentanone, hence status 'rejected' with relative_intensity 0.005. ARC COUNT: Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn - the arc from the C(1)-C(2) sigma bond into the C(2)-C(3) bond and the arc from the odd electron of the pi-ionized carbonyl into that same C(2)-C(3) bond (their two barbs are printed side by side between CH2 and C) - and move <3>, the sigma-bond electron that leaves with the methyl, is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page; the book simply writes CH3. among the products). LOCALIZATION NOTE (convention B/C): the page draws the ionized carbonyl with a SINGLE C-O bond and one '+.' superscript between C and O. Split for balance and to match the text, the odd electron sits on the carbonyl carbon C(3) (the arrow's origin) and the charge on the monovalent oxygen O(4); the product written here, CH2=C(C2H5)-O(+), is the canonical form the arrows actually produce and the one printed on the left of the book's resonance arrow, its partner (+)CH2-C(C2H5)=O being drawn on the right.

No MOD rule is cross-linked: rule_index.json has no 'by_equation' entry for 4.16, and the rule module states verbatim '# 4.16 not included as it is a negative example (example cleavage impossible)' (IMS_chap4_examples.py:376, repeated at the fragmentation list, line 1152). That is the intended state - the record is kept as a labelled negative/disfavored pathway, not as a generator rule. RDKit bookkeeping note: RDKit assigns the monovalent [O+] two radical electrons in both states (an artifact of its valence model); the change is zero, so the arrow bookkeeping is unaffected, and the declared electronic state (charge +1, 0 unpaired for the closed-shell product ion) is the chemically correct one.
